newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LITHUANIA - SHARES EASE, GAINS NOT SEEN.
newsitem.headline: LITHUANIA - SHARES EASE, GAINS NOT SEEN.

text.p: Lithuanian shares eased on Wednesday and dealers were not bullish about the bourse's immediate prospects.
Dealers said that buyers were bargain hunting and staying on the sidelines in the hopes that prices would fall further.
"Investors are waiting for prices to fall more, and they seem to be getting their wish...there probably won't be much in the way of gains this week," said one dealer.
Losers included tractor parts producer Kura aparatura, which saw its price ease to 8.20 litas from 9.10 litas.
Dealers said the market was responding to its first quarter resluts, which showed a steep fall in its net profit to 207,730 litas from 6.9 million litas for the same period last year.
The company exports much of its production to CIS countries and many of its customers have failed to pay their bills.
Defying the gloomy trend, Siauliu Bank rose ten percent for the third straight session, advancing to 93.17 litas from 84.70 litas in trade of 37,000 litas.
Dealers said its price was being driven up by Hermis Bank's announcement last week that it planned to acquire 51 percent of the bank's shares.
